name: A Radius-Two Vertex in a Tree Reduction Retains Its Fibre
statement: Let $X$ be ample and suppose an active-coordinate reduction $D$ is a tree. If every vertex of $D$ is within graph distance two of $z$, then the following are equivalent: one lift of $z$ is an attainable endpoint; $X$ peels to the entire two-point fibre over $z$; both lifts are attainable. Hence a nonretainable coordinate edge with an attainable endpoint projects to a vertex of eccentricity at least three in any tree reduction. For a four-vertex path it must project to an endpoint, and the bound is sharp.
proof: Induct on the size of the reduction. Star reductions are the base case. In an endpoint peeling, the first deletion over the still-intact reduction projects to a tree corner and therefore to a leaf different from $z$. Removing that fibre vertex leaves an ample expansion whose reduction is the tree with this leaf deleted; distances among surviving vertices are unchanged and the endpoint-order suffix remains valid. Induction retains the whole fibre over $z$. The remaining implications and eccentricity consequence are immediate.
